about: Ember's problem library. "problems" are stated in her typed language: each task is a problem she can run with autonomous_research, and the query open_problems lets her choose one herself. "catalog" lists open problems she cannot state yet; each names what her language lacks, described under "needs". Her choice reads only the id, status and task of a stated problem. Titles, statements, scopes, known results, sources and the catalog are for people: they were written from secondary knowledge, statuses were checked by web search where "checked" says so, and none of it is evidence she uses.

problems.title: Erdős–Straus conjecture
problems.statement: For every integer n >= 2, 4/n = 1/x + 1/y + 1/z has a solution in positive integers.
problems.scope: Her theorems prove the statement for every n from the least n outside the residue classes her covers leave open, and her range checks every n below 100,000. Her own checked lemma shows that no classical fixed-parameter family reaches a coprime square class, so for 4/n covers of this kind cannot settle it.
problems.known: Open. Mordell showed it for every n outside six residue classes mod 840 (the squares 1, 121, 169, 289, 361, 529). Her Campaign 1 reduced it to 26,262 classes mod 36,756,720 (CAMPAIGNS.md).
problems.source: Erdős and Straus (1948); Mordell, Diophantine Equations (1969).

problems.title: Sierpiński's 5/n conjecture
problems.statement: For every integer n >= 2, 5/n = 1/x + 1/y + 1/z has a solution in positive integers.
problems.scope: Her theorems prove the statement for every n from the least n outside the residue classes her covers leave open, and her range checks every n below 100,000. Her own checked lemma shows that no classical fixed-parameter family reaches a coprime square class, but for 5/n her checker refuted that lemma; covers of this kind cannot settle it.
problems.known: Open. Her Campaign 2 reduced it to 821 classes mod 8,031,343,320 (CAMPAIGNS.md). Secondary sources say it is settled except possibly for n ≡ 1 (mod 278,460).

problems.title: Schinzel's conjecture for 6/n
problems.statement: For every integer n >= 2, 6/n = 1/x + 1/y + 1/z has a solution in positive integers.
problems.scope: Her theorems prove the statement for every n from the least n outside the residue classes her covers leave open, and her range checks every n below 100,000.
problems.known: Open for a = 6 as for every a >= 4. For even n = 2m, 6/n = 3/m, which is always a sum of three unit fractions.
problems.source: The conjecture that for every fixed a, a/n = 1/x + 1/y + 1/z for all sufficiently large n is attributed to Schinzel; Sierpiński (1956) posed a = 5.

problems.title: Schinzel's conjecture for 7/n
problems.statement: For every integer n >= 3, 7/n = 1/x + 1/y + 1/z has a solution in positive integers.
problems.scope: Her theorems prove the statement for every n from the least n outside the residue classes her covers leave open, and her range checks every n below 100,000.
problems.known: Open for a = 7 as for every a >= 4. An exhaustive search in this environment found no representation for n = 2 and one for every other n below 20,000, so the statement starts at n = 3.
problems.source: The conjecture that for every fixed a, a/n = 1/x + 1/y + 1/z for all sufficiently large n is attributed to Schinzel; Sierpiński (1956) posed a = 5.

problems.known: Open for a = 8 as for every a >= 4. For even n = 2m, 8/n = 4/m: its even members are the Erdős–Straus conjecture for m = n/2.
problems.source: The conjecture that for every fixed a, a/n = 1/x + 1/y + 1/z for all sufficiently large n is attributed to Schinzel; Sierpiński (1956) posed a = 5.

problems.title: Collatz conjecture
problems.statement: Every orbit of T(n) = n/2 (n even), (3n + 1)/2 (n odd) from a positive integer reaches 1.
problems.scope: Her descent covers prove that every n in a covered class modulo 2^20 falls below itself, and her range checks every n below 10^6. The class of 2^k - 1 modulo 2^k never descends within k steps, so no finite depth settles the conjecture in this language.
problems.known: Open. Verified by computer far beyond her range; Tao (2019) proved that almost all orbits attain almost bounded values.
problems.source: Collatz (1937); Lagarias, The 3x + 1 Problem and Its Generalizations (1985).

problems.title: The Collatz stopping-time sieve to 2^18
problems.statement: Count the residue classes modulo 2^k, for k = 1 to 18, on which T^j(n) < n is not certified within k steps.
problems.scope: A closed count: her open classes at each level can be compared with an independent parity simulation.
problems.known: Closed. 7,495 classes mod 2^18 stay open; her Campaign 3 matched all 18 levels against an independent count.
problems.source: The stopping-time sieve is classical (Terras 1976; Everett 1977).

problems.title: Three unit fractions for 3/n
problems.statement: For every integer n >= 2, 3/n = 1/x + 1/y + 1/z has a solution in positive integers.
problems.scope: A theorem with no open residue proves the statement for every n >= 2.
problems.known: True: 3/n = 1/n + 1/n + 1/n. A calibration of the settled path for covers.

problems.title: Descent of the halving map
problems.statement: Under T(n) = n/2 (n even), (n + 1)/2 (n odd), every n >= 2 has some j >= 1 with T^j(n) < n.
problems.scope: A descent cover reaching every class of its modulus, with a range from 2 to its bound, proves the statement.
problems.known: True in one step. A calibration of the settled path for descent.

problems.title: Descent of the 3n - 1 map
problems.statement: Under T(n) = n/2 (n even), (3n - 1)/2 (n odd), every n >= 2 has some j >= 1 with T^j(n) < n.
problems.scope: A checked cycle avoiding 1 refutes the statement: its least member never falls below itself.
problems.known: False: 5 -> 7 -> 10 -> 5 is a cycle. Refutation practice.

problems.title: Descent of the 5n + 1 map
problems.statement: Under T(n) = n/2 (n even), (5n + 1)/2 (n odd), every n >= 2 has some j >= 1 with T^j(n) < n.
problems.scope: A checked cycle avoiding 1 refutes the statement: its least member never falls below itself.
problems.known: False: 13 -> 33 -> 83 -> 208 -> 104 -> 52 -> 26 -> 13 is a cycle. Refutation practice. Whether the orbit of 7 is unbounded is open and listed in the catalog.

catalog.title: Riemann hypothesis
catalog.statement: Every nontrivial zero of the Riemann zeta function has real part 1/2.
catalog.source: Riemann (1859); a Clay Millennium Prize Problem (2000).

catalog.title: Generalized Riemann hypothesis
catalog.statement: Every nontrivial zero of every Dirichlet L-function has real part 1/2.

catalog.title: Goldbach's conjecture
catalog.statement: Every even integer greater than 2 is the sum of two primes.
catalog.source: Goldbach, letter to Euler (1742). The ternary version was proved by Helfgott (2013).
catalog.nearest: A claim kind "every even n in [4, N) is a sum of two primes", checked with one witness per n, would let her check finite ranges; the conjecture itself needs more.

catalog.title: Twin prime conjecture
catalog.statement: There are infinitely many primes p such that p + 2 is also prime.
catalog.source: Stated by de Polignac (1849). Bounded gaps: Zhang (2013), Maynard (2015), Polymath8.

catalog.title: Polignac's conjecture
catalog.statement: For every even k, infinitely many pairs of consecutive primes differ by exactly k.

catalog.title: Legendre's conjecture
catalog.statement: For every positive integer n there is a prime between n^2 and (n + 1)^2.
catalog.source: Legendre; one of the four problems Landau listed in 1912.
catalog.nearest: A claim kind "for every n in [1, N) a prime lies in (n^2, (n+1)^2)", checked with one witness per n, would state finite ranges.

catalog.title: Primes of the form n^2 + 1
catalog.statement: There are infinitely many primes of the form n^2 + 1.
catalog.source: Landau (1912), one of his four problems.

catalog.title: Andrica's conjecture
catalog.statement: For consecutive primes p < q, sqrt(q) - sqrt(p) < 1.

catalog.title: Oppermann's conjecture
catalog.statement: For every integer n > 1 there is a prime between n(n - 1) and n^2, and another between n^2 and n(n + 1).

catalog.title: Cramér's conjecture
catalog.statement: Gaps between consecutive primes satisfy p_(n+1) - p_n = O((log p_n)^2).

catalog.title: Infinitely many Mersenne primes
catalog.statement: There are infinitely many primes of the form 2^p - 1 (equivalently, infinitely many even perfect numbers).
catalog.source: Mersenne (1644); the question of infinitude is folklore.

catalog.title: Fermat primes beyond 65537
catalog.statement: Is 2^(2^n) + 1 composite for every n > 4? (Only n = 0..4 give known primes.)
catalog.source: Fermat (1640) conjectured all are prime; Euler (1732) factored the case n = 5.

catalog.title: Infinitely many Sophie Germain primes
catalog.statement: There are infinitely many primes p such that 2p + 1 is also prime.
catalog.source: Folklore; implied by the Hardy-Littlewood prime tuples conjecture.

catalog.title: Schinzel's Hypothesis H
catalog.statement: If irreducible integer polynomials f_1, ..., f_k with positive leading coefficients have no fixed prime divisor of their product, then infinitely many n make every f_i(n) prime.

catalog.title: Bunyakovsky conjecture
catalog.statement: An irreducible integer polynomial with positive leading coefficient and no fixed prime divisor takes infinitely many prime values.

catalog.title: Hardy-Littlewood prime k-tuples conjecture
catalog.statement: Every admissible pattern of k linear forms n + h_i is simultaneously prime infinitely often, with the asymptotic count predicted by the singular series.

catalog.title: Artin's primitive root conjecture
catalog.statement: Every integer other than -1 that is not a perfect square is a primitive root modulo infinitely many primes.
catalog.source: Artin (1927); proved under the generalized Riemann hypothesis by Hooley (1967).

catalog.title: Infinitely many Wieferich primes
catalog.statement: There are infinitely many primes p with p^2 dividing 2^(p-1) - 1. Only 1093 and 3511 are known.

catalog.title: Wall-Sun-Sun primes
catalog.statement: Is there a prime p such that p^2 divides the Fibonacci number F(p - (p/5))? None is known.

catalog.title: Gilbreath's conjecture
catalog.statement: Repeatedly taking absolute differences of consecutive terms, starting from the sequence of primes, every row after the first begins with 1.

catalog.title: Infinitely many regular primes
catalog.statement: There are infinitely many regular primes (primes not dividing the class number of the p-th cyclotomic field).
catalog.source: Kummer (1850); Jensen (1915) proved there are infinitely many irregular primes.

catalog.title: Infinitely many Fibonacci primes
catalog.statement: Infinitely many Fibonacci numbers are prime.

catalog.title: Brocard's problem
catalog.statement: n! + 1 = m^2 has no integer solutions other than n = 4, 5 and 7.

catalog.title: Erdős-Moser equation
catalog.statement: 1^k + 2^k + ... + (m - 1)^k = m^k has no solution in positive integers other than 1 + 2 = 3.

catalog.title: Odd perfect numbers
catalog.statement: There is no odd perfect number (no odd n with sigma(n) = 2n).

catalog.title: Lehmer's totient problem
catalog.statement: No composite n has phi(n) dividing n - 1.

catalog.title: Carmichael's totient conjecture
catalog.statement: For every m, the equation phi(x) = m has either no solution or at least two.

catalog.title: Infinitely many amicable pairs
catalog.statement: There are infinitely many pairs m < n with sigma(m) = sigma(n) = m + n.

catalog.title: Odd weird numbers
catalog.statement: Is there an odd weird number (abundant, but not a sum of any subset of its proper divisors)?

catalog.title: Catalan-Dickson conjecture on aliquot sequences
catalog.statement: Every aliquot sequence n, s(n), s(s(n)), ... with s(n) = sigma(n) - n ends at 0 or becomes periodic. The sequence from 276 is not known to end.
catalog.source: Catalan (1888), Dickson (1913); Guy and Selfridge conjectured the opposite.

catalog.title: The 196 problem
catalog.statement: Repeatedly adding 196 to the reversal of its decimal digits never produces a palindrome.

catalog.title: Perfect cuboid
catalog.statement: There is no rectangular box whose three edges, three face diagonals and space diagonal are all integers.

catalog.title: abc conjecture
catalog.statement: For every epsilon > 0, only finitely many coprime triples a + b = c satisfy c > rad(abc)^(1 + epsilon).
catalog.source: Masser (1985) and Oesterlé (1988). Mochizuki (2012) announced a proof that is not accepted by most experts (Scholze and Stix, 2018).

catalog.title: Beal conjecture
catalog.statement: If A^x + B^y = C^z with positive integers and x, y, z > 2, then A, B and C share a prime factor.

catalog.title: Fermat-Catalan conjecture
catalog.statement: The equation a^m + b^n = c^k with coprime positive a, b, c and 1/m + 1/n + 1/k < 1 has only finitely many solutions (counting each (a^m, b^n, c^k) once).

catalog.title: Pillai's conjecture
catalog.statement: Each positive integer occurs only finitely many times as a difference of two perfect powers.

catalog.title: Sums of three cubes
catalog.statement: Every integer n not congruent to 4 or 5 mod 9 is a sum of three integer cubes.
catalog.source: Heath-Brown (1992) conjectured it with infinitely many representations; 33 and 42 were found in 2019 (Booker; Booker and Sutherland).

catalog.title: Congruent number problem
catalog.statement: Decide for every n whether n is the area of a right triangle with rational sides. Tunnell (1983) gave a criterion that is complete if the Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture holds for y^2 = x^3 - n^2 x.

catalog.title: Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture
catalog.statement: The rank of an elliptic curve over Q equals the order of vanishing of its L-function at s = 1.
catalog.source: Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer (1960s); a Clay Millennium Prize Problem.

catalog.title: Kummer-Vandiver conjecture
catalog.statement: For every prime p, p does not divide the class number of the maximal real subfield of the p-th cyclotomic field.

catalog.title: Leopoldt's conjecture
catalog.statement: The p-adic regulator of a number field is nonzero.

catalog.title: Infinitely many real quadratic fields of class number one
catalog.statement: Infinitely many real quadratic fields have class number 1.

catalog.title: Lehmer's Mahler measure problem
catalog.statement: There is a constant c > 1 such that every integer polynomial that is not a product of cyclotomic polynomials and powers of x has Mahler measure at least c.

catalog.title: Littlewood conjecture
catalog.statement: For all real a and b, liminf over n of n * ||n a|| * ||n b|| is 0, where ||x|| is the distance to the nearest integer.
catalog.source: Littlewood (about 1930); Einsiedler, Katok and Lindenstrauss (2006) proved the exceptions have Hausdorff dimension 0.

catalog.title: Mahler's 3/2 problem
catalog.statement: Is there a real x > 0 such that the fractional part of x (3/2)^n lies in [0, 1/2) for every n >= 0?

catalog.title: Gauss circle problem
catalog.statement: The number of lattice points in the disc of radius r is pi r^2 + O(r^(1/2 + epsilon)) for every epsilon > 0.
catalog.source: Gauss; Hardy (1915) showed that 1/2 cannot be lowered.

catalog.title: Dirichlet divisor problem
catalog.statement: The sum of d(n) for n <= x equals x log x + (2 gamma - 1) x + O(x^(1/4 + epsilon)) for every epsilon > 0.

catalog.title: Lindelöf hypothesis
catalog.statement: For every epsilon > 0, zeta(1/2 + i t) = O(|t|^epsilon).
catalog.source: Lindelöf (1908); implied by the Riemann hypothesis.

catalog.title: The value of G(3) in Waring's problem
catalog.statement: Every sufficiently large integer is a sum of four positive cubes (G(3) = 4; known: 4 <= G(3) <= 7).

catalog.title: Is 78,557 the smallest Sierpiński number?
catalog.statement: For every odd k < 78,557 there is an n with k 2^n + 1 prime. A few k remain without a known prime.
catalog.source: Sierpiński (1960); Selfridge (1962) found the covering for 78,557.

catalog.title: Is 509,203 the smallest Riesel number?
catalog.statement: For every odd k < 509,203 there is an n with k 2^n - 1 prime.

catalog.title: Covering systems with odd moduli
catalog.statement: Is there a finite covering system of the integers whose moduli are distinct odd integers greater than 1?
catalog.source: Erdős and Selfridge. Hough (2015) bounded the least modulus of a distinct covering system.
catalog.nearest: A claim kind for a covering system (a finite list of residue classes whose union is all integers, checked at the lcm of the moduli) is close to her language; existence would then be a search, nonexistence needs more.

catalog.title: Schinzel's conjecture for numerators 12, 15, 16 and above 16
catalog.statement: For every fixed a, a/n = 1/x + 1/y + 1/z has a solution in positive integers for all sufficiently large n. For a = 12, 15 and 16 an exhaustive search here found exceptions beyond n = 1000, and numerators above 16 lie beyond her statement bounds.

catalog.title: Divergent orbits of the 5x + 1 map
catalog.statement: The orbit of 7 under T(n) = n/2 (n even), (5n + 1)/2 (n odd) is unbounded.
catalog.source: Folklore around the Collatz problem (see Lagarias, The 3x + 1 Problem and Its Generalizations, 1985).

catalog.title: Conway's amusical permutation
catalog.statement: Under g(2n) = 3n, g(4n + 1) = 3n + 1, g(4n - 1) = 3n - 1, is the orbit of 8 infinite?

catalog.title: The sixth Busy Beaver value
catalog.statement: Determine BB(6), the most steps a halting 6-state, 2-symbol Turing machine takes from a blank tape. Some holdout machines encode Collatz-like problems.
catalog.source: Radó (1962); BB(5) = 47,176,870 was proved by the bbchallenge collaboration (2024).

catalog.title: Erdős conjecture on arithmetic progressions
catalog.statement: If the sum of 1/a over a set A of positive integers diverges, A contains arithmetic progressions of every length.
catalog.source: Erdős (1936 with Turán, and later); length 3 proved by Bloom and Sisask (2020).

catalog.title: Erdős-Turán conjecture on additive bases
catalog.statement: If every positive integer is a sum of two elements of B, then the number of such representations is unbounded.

catalog.title: Largest Sidon sets
catalog.statement: The largest Sidon subset of {1, ..., n} has size sqrt(n) + O(n^epsilon) for every epsilon > 0 (Erdős asked whether even sqrt(n) + O(1) holds).

catalog.title: Erdős-Szemerédi sum-product conjecture
catalog.statement: For every epsilon > 0 and every finite set A of integers, max(|A + A|, |A A|) >= c |A|^(2 - epsilon).

catalog.title: Singmaster's conjecture
catalog.statement: There is a finite bound on how many times an integer greater than 1 appears in Pascal's triangle.

catalog.title: Erdős unit distance problem
catalog.statement: The number of unit distances among n points in the plane is at most n^(1 + O(1/log log n)).

catalog.title: Heilbronn triangle problem
catalog.statement: Determine the order of the largest possible smallest triangle area among n points in the unit square.

catalog.title: No-three-in-line problem
catalog.statement: For all large n, can 2n points of the n x n grid be chosen with no three collinear?

catalog.title: Erdős-Szekeres conjecture (happy ending problem)
catalog.statement: Every set of 2^(n-2) + 1 points in the plane in general position contains the vertices of a convex n-gon.
catalog.source: Erdős and Szekeres (1935); proved for n <= 6; Suk (2017) proved 2^(n + o(n)).

catalog.title: Chromatic number of the plane
catalog.statement: Determine the least number of colors needed so that no two points at distance 1 share a color. Known: 5, 6 or 7.
catalog.source: Nelson (1950); de Grey (2018) proved at least 5.

catalog.title: Kissing number in dimension 5
catalog.statement: Determine the largest number of non-overlapping unit spheres in R^5 that touch a common unit sphere (40 to 44).
catalog.source: Folklore; bounds from lattice constructions and semidefinite programming.

catalog.title: Densest sphere packings in other dimensions
catalog.statement: Determine the densest sphere packing in R^n for n other than 1, 2, 3, 8 and 24.
catalog.source: Kepler (1611); Hales (2005) for n = 3; Viazovska (2016) for n = 8, with coauthors for n = 24.

catalog.title: Inscribed square problem
catalog.statement: Every Jordan curve in the plane contains the four vertices of a square.

catalog.title: Moving sofa problem
catalog.statement: Determine the largest area of a planar shape that can be moved around a right-angled corner in a hallway of unit width. Gerver (1992) gave a shape of area about 2.2195.

catalog.title: Kakeya conjecture in higher dimensions
catalog.statement: Every Besicovitch set in R^n (containing a unit segment in every direction) has Hausdorff dimension n.
catalog.source: Kakeya (1917), Besicovitch (1919); proved for n = 2 by Davies (1971).

catalog.title: Fourier restriction conjecture
catalog.statement: The Fourier extension operator from the unit sphere in R^n is bounded from L^infinity to L^p for every p > 2n/(n - 1).

catalog.title: Bochner-Riesz conjecture
catalog.statement: The Bochner-Riesz means of order delta > 0 are bounded on L^p(R^n) exactly in the conjectured range of p.

catalog.title: Heesch's problem
catalog.statement: Which positive integers are Heesch numbers of plane shapes, and is there an upper bound?

catalog.title: Lonely runner conjecture
catalog.statement: For k runners with distinct constant speeds on a unit circular track, each runner is at some time at distance at least 1/k from all the others.

catalog.title: Thomson problem
catalog.statement: Determine the configuration of n unit charges on a sphere minimizing electrostatic energy, for all n.

catalog.title: Erdős-Ulam problem
catalog.statement: Is there a dense set of points in the plane with all pairwise distances rational?

catalog.title: Borsuk's problem in dimensions 4 to 63
catalog.statement: Can every bounded set in R^n be partitioned into n + 1 sets of smaller diameter? False for n >= 64, true for n <= 3.
catalog.source: Borsuk (1933); Kahn and Kalai (1993) found the first counterexamples.

catalog.title: Mahler's conjecture on the volume product
catalog.statement: The product of the volumes of a centrally symmetric convex body and its polar body is minimized by the cube.
catalog.source: Mahler (1939); proved in dimension 3 by Iriyeh and Shibata (2020).

catalog.title: Hadwiger covering conjecture
catalog.statement: Every convex body in R^n can be covered by 2^n smaller homothetic copies of itself.

catalog.title: Hadwiger's conjecture
catalog.statement: Every graph with no K_t minor is (t - 1)-colorable.

catalog.title: Erdős-Hajnal conjecture
catalog.statement: For every graph H there is c > 0 such that every n-vertex graph without an induced copy of H has a clique or an independent set of size n^c.

catalog.title: Graceful tree conjecture
catalog.statement: Every tree has a graceful labeling.

catalog.title: Cycle double cover conjecture
catalog.statement: Every bridgeless graph has a family of cycles covering each edge exactly twice.

catalog.title: Reconstruction conjecture
catalog.statement: Every graph with at least three vertices is determined up to isomorphism by its multiset of vertex-deleted subgraphs.

catalog.title: Seymour's second neighborhood conjecture
catalog.statement: Every oriented graph has a vertex whose second out-neighborhood is at least as large as its first.

catalog.title: Caccetta-Häggkvist conjecture
catalog.statement: Every directed graph on n vertices with minimum out-degree r has a directed cycle of length at most ceil(n/r).

catalog.title: Total coloring conjecture
catalog.statement: Every graph of maximum degree D has a total coloring with at most D + 2 colors.

catalog.title: List edge-coloring conjecture
catalog.statement: The list chromatic index of every graph equals its chromatic index.

catalog.title: Lovász conjecture on vertex-transitive graphs
catalog.statement: Every finite connected vertex-transitive graph has a Hamiltonian path.

catalog.title: Barnette's conjecture
catalog.statement: Every cubic, bipartite, 3-connected planar graph is Hamiltonian.

catalog.title: Erdős-Gyárfás conjecture
catalog.statement: Every graph with minimum degree at least 3 contains a cycle whose length is a power of 2.

catalog.title: Conway's 99-graph problem
catalog.statement: Is there a strongly regular graph with parameters (99, 14, 1, 2)?

catalog.title: Moore graph of degree 57
catalog.statement: Is there a 57-regular graph of diameter 2 and girth 5 on 3250 vertices?

catalog.title: Sidorenko's conjecture
catalog.statement: For every bipartite graph H, the density of H in any graph of edge density p is at least p^(e(H)).

catalog.title: Graham's pebbling conjecture
catalog.statement: The pebbling number of a Cartesian product satisfies pi(G x H) <= pi(G) pi(H).

catalog.title: The Ramsey number R(5, 5)
catalog.statement: Determine R(5, 5), the least n such that every 2-coloring of the edges of K_n has a monochromatic K_5.
catalog.source: Greenwood and Gleason (1955) for small cases; Exoo (1989) for the lower bound 43.

catalog.title: The sixth Schur number
catalog.statement: Determine S(6), the largest n such that {1, ..., n} can be split into six sum-free parts.
catalog.source: Schur (1916); S(5) = 160 was proved with a SAT solver by Heule (2017).

catalog.title: Union-closed sets conjecture
catalog.statement: Every finite union-closed family with a nonempty member has an element in at least half of its members.
catalog.source: Frankl (1979); Gilmer (2022) proved a constant fraction.

catalog.title: Sunflower conjecture
catalog.statement: There is C(k) such that every family of more than C(k)^w sets of size w contains a sunflower with k petals.
catalog.source: Erdős and Rado (1960); Alweiss, Lovett, Wu and Zhang (2019) improved the bound.

catalog.title: 1/3-2/3 conjecture
catalog.statement: Every finite partial order that is not a chain has two elements x, y with 1/3 <= P(x before y) <= 2/3 in a uniformly random linear extension.

catalog.title: Rota's basis conjecture
catalog.statement: For n bases of a rank-n matroid, the n^2 elements can be arranged in an n x n grid whose rows are the bases and whose columns are also bases.

catalog.title: Chvátal's conjecture
catalog.statement: In every down-closed family of sets, some largest intersecting subfamily consists of the sets containing one common element.

catalog.title: Hadamard conjecture
catalog.statement: A Hadamard matrix of order 4k exists for every positive integer k.

catalog.title: Projective plane of order 12
catalog.statement: Is there a finite projective plane of order 12? (Order 10 was excluded by computer in 1989.)
catalog.source: Lam, Thiel and Swiercz (1989) for order 10.

catalog.title: Three mutually orthogonal Latin squares of order 10
catalog.statement: Are there three mutually orthogonal Latin squares of order 10?
catalog.source: Euler's 36 officers problem and its successors; Parker, Bose and Shrikhande (1959) disproved Euler for order 10 with two squares.

catalog.title: Inverse Galois problem
catalog.statement: Every finite group is the Galois group of some Galois extension of the rational numbers.

catalog.title: Jacobian conjecture
catalog.statement: A polynomial map from C^n to C^n with constant nonzero Jacobian determinant has a polynomial inverse.

catalog.title: Kaplansky zero-divisor conjecture
catalog.statement: The group ring K[G] of a torsion-free group G over a field K has no zero divisors. (The related unit conjecture was disproved by Gardam in 2021.)

catalog.title: Is the Burnside group B(2, 5) finite?
catalog.statement: Is the free Burnside group on two generators of exponent 5 finite?

catalog.title: Andrews-Curtis conjecture
catalog.statement: Every balanced presentation of the trivial group can be reduced to the trivial presentation by Andrews-Curtis moves.

catalog.title: Whitehead asphericity conjecture
catalog.statement: Every connected subcomplex of an aspherical 2-dimensional CW complex is aspherical.

catalog.title: Smooth four-dimensional Poincaré conjecture
catalog.statement: Every smooth 4-manifold homotopy equivalent to the 4-sphere is diffeomorphic to it.

catalog.title: Volume conjecture
catalog.statement: For a hyperbolic knot K, 2 pi log |J_N(K; e^(2 pi i/N))| / N tends to the hyperbolic volume of its complement.
catalog.source: Kashaev (1997); H. Murakami and J. Murakami (2001).

catalog.title: Hodge conjecture
catalog.statement: On a non-singular complex projective variety, every rational Hodge class is a rational combination of classes of algebraic cycles.
catalog.source: Hodge (1950); a Clay Millennium Prize Problem.

catalog.title: Grothendieck's standard conjectures
catalog.statement: The standard conjectures on algebraic cycles (Lefschetz type and Hodge type) hold for smooth projective varieties.

catalog.title: Tate conjecture
catalog.statement: For a smooth projective variety over a finitely generated field, the Galois-invariant l-adic cohomology classes are spanned by algebraic cycles.

catalog.title: Resolution of singularities in positive characteristic
catalog.statement: Every variety over a field of positive characteristic admits a resolution of singularities, in all dimensions.

catalog.title: Navier-Stokes existence and smoothness
catalog.statement: For smooth, rapidly decaying initial data, the incompressible Navier-Stokes equations in R^3 have smooth solutions for all time (or give a counterexample).

catalog.title: Yang-Mills existence and mass gap
catalog.statement: For every compact simple gauge group, quantum Yang-Mills theory on R^4 exists and has a mass gap.

catalog.title: Sendov's conjecture
catalog.statement: If all zeros of a complex polynomial of degree at least 2 lie in the closed unit disc, each zero is within distance 1 of a zero of its derivative.
catalog.source: Sendov (1958); Tao (2020) proved it for sufficiently large degree.

catalog.title: Casas-Alvero conjecture
catalog.statement: A complex polynomial of degree n that shares a root with each of its first n - 1 derivatives is (x - a)^n.

catalog.title: Hot spots conjecture
catalog.statement: For a bounded Lipschitz domain, the maximum and minimum of the second Neumann eigenfunction are attained on the boundary.

catalog.title: Schiffer's conjecture
catalog.statement: If a Neumann eigenfunction on a bounded planar domain is constant on the boundary, the domain is a disc.
catalog.source: Schiffer (1950s); related to the Pompeiu problem.

catalog.title: Invariant subspace problem
catalog.statement: Every bounded operator on a separable infinite-dimensional complex Hilbert space has a nontrivial closed invariant subspace.
catalog.source: Folklore; false for some Banach spaces (Enflo; Read).

catalog.title: Hilbert's sixteenth problem (second part)
catalog.statement: Bound the number of limit cycles of a planar polynomial vector field of degree n in terms of n.

catalog.title: Local connectivity of the Mandelbrot set
catalog.statement: The Mandelbrot set is locally connected.

catalog.title: Furstenberg x2 x3 conjecture
catalog.statement: The only ergodic probability measures on the circle invariant under both x -> 2x and x -> 3x are Lebesgue measure and measures supported on finite orbits.

catalog.title: Irrationality of e + pi
catalog.statement: Is e + pi irrational? (At least one of e + pi and e pi is transcendental.)

catalog.title: Irrationality of the Euler-Mascheroni constant
catalog.statement: Is gamma = 0.5772... irrational?

catalog.title: Irrationality of Catalan's constant
catalog.statement: Is G = 0.9159... irrational?

catalog.title: Irrationality of zeta(5)
catalog.statement: Is zeta(5) irrational? (Apéry proved zeta(3) irrational in 1978; Zudilin (2001) showed one of zeta(5), zeta(7), zeta(9), zeta(11) is irrational.)

catalog.title: Normality of pi
catalog.statement: Every block of k decimal digits occurs in the expansion of pi with limiting frequency 10^(-k).

catalog.title: Schanuel's conjecture
catalog.statement: For complex z_1, ..., z_n linearly independent over Q, the field Q(z_1, ..., z_n, e^(z_1), ..., e^(z_n)) has transcendence degree at least n.

catalog.title: Four exponentials conjecture
catalog.statement: If x_1, x_2 and y_1, y_2 are each linearly independent over Q, then one of the four numbers e^(x_i y_j) is transcendental.

catalog.title: P versus NP
catalog.statement: Is every problem whose solutions can be verified in polynomial time also solvable in polynomial time?
catalog.source: Cook (1971), Levin (1973); a Clay Millennium Prize Problem.

catalog.title: NP versus coNP
catalog.statement: Is NP closed under complement?

catalog.title: Derandomization of BPP
catalog.statement: Does BPP equal P?

catalog.title: Graph isomorphism in polynomial time
catalog.statement: Can graph isomorphism be decided in polynomial time? Babai (2015) gave a quasi-polynomial algorithm.

catalog.title: The exponent of matrix multiplication
catalog.statement: Is omega = 2, that is, can n x n matrices be multiplied in O(n^(2 + epsilon)) operations for every epsilon > 0?

catalog.title: Unique games conjecture
catalog.statement: For every epsilon > 0 it is NP-hard to distinguish unique games that are (1 - epsilon)-satisfiable from those that are at most epsilon-satisfiable.
catalog.source: Khot (2002); the 2-to-2 case was proved in 2018.

needs.infinitude: A checked certificate that infinitely many integers have a property. Her checker admits finite certificates, identities on residue classes and descent on classes; none of them yields an unbounded supply of primes or solutions.
needs.prime-distribution: Explicit estimates for primes in intervals or progressions (sieve bounds with explicit constants, prime tables beyond her ranges).
needs.arithmetic-functions: Claims about sigma(n), phi(n) and other arithmetic functions for all n, beyond finite ranges.
needs.diophantine: Finiteness or nonexistence of integer solutions beyond identities on residue classes: curves of genus one and higher, exponential equations, height bounds.
needs.diophantine-approximation: Statements about how well real numbers are approximated by rationals, for all real parameters.
needs.algebraic-number-theory: Number fields, class groups, units and cyclotomic arithmetic.
needs.analytic: Complex analysis: L-functions and their zeros, contour estimates, conformal maps, zeros of polynomials.
needs.transcendence: Irrationality or transcendence certificates for specific constants.
needs.digits-normality: Statements about the digit distribution of constants.
needs.real-analysis: Inequalities, limits and extremal problems over the real numbers.
needs.harmonic-analysis: Fourier restriction, maximal functions and Kakeya-type estimates.
needs.pde: Existence, regularity and spectral properties of partial differential equations.
needs.algebraic-geometry: Varieties, cohomology theories and algebraic cycles.
needs.algebra: Rings, polynomial maps, fields and Galois groups.
needs.groups: Group presentations, finiteness questions and representations.
needs.topology: Manifolds, knots, homotopy and four-dimensional topology.
needs.geometry: Points, distances, packings, coverings and convex bodies in Euclidean space.
needs.graphs: Graphs with colorings, minors, labelings, cycles and Hamiltonian paths.
needs.set-systems: Families of sets, hypergraphs, partial orders and matroids.
needs.additive-combinatorics: Sums, products and arithmetic progressions in sets of integers, for all sets.
needs.finite-search-at-scale: A finite question whose resolution needs a search far beyond her work bounds, with a checkable certificate such as a SAT proof log or an exhaustive-search receipt.
needs.big-integers: Primality proofs and arithmetic for integers far beyond her bounds.
needs.unbounded-orbits: A certificate that an orbit never terminates or grows without bound; her descent language certifies only that orbits fall.
needs.dynamics: Continuous, holomorphic or measure-theoretic dynamical systems.
needs.complexity: Computational complexity classes and lower bounds.
needs.operator-theory: Operators on infinite-dimensional Hilbert and Banach spaces.
needs.designs: Combinatorial designs: Hadamard matrices, projective planes, orthogonal Latin squares.
needs.mathematical-physics: Rigorous quantum field theory and fluid equations.
needs.covering-systems: Finite systems of congruences covering the integers. Her language has residue classes but no claim kind for a covering system.
needs.statement-bounds: Stateable with her current claim kinds, but beyond the bounds of her problem statements (numerator at most 16, three terms, least n at most 1000, lifted modulus at most 10^6).
